standard_feature_contracts.applies_to: Every app built from a templates entry in this registry, and every future base created for a key listed in missing. Predicates are dual-dialect: each check names the canon-base mechanism and/or the shipped flagship mechanism (the one-system os-* dialect, live at naya-model-*.nayapower.workers.dev). A feature passes on the mechanism the surface actually ships, never on a label alone. Where a canon selector names a Hub-room surface and the flagship realizes the same feature as an in-page block, the predicate is scoped to that block; see per-feature applies_to and dialect_note.
standard_feature_contracts.dialect_note: Dialect reconciliation (GT-028, 2026-10-22): the v1 predicates were authored against the canon-base dialect only, so the shipped flagships scored 4/13 while demonstrably carrying most features in the one-system os-* dialect. v1.1 names both dialects, verified byte-by-byte against the three live models (301,792 / 301,729 / 301,774 bytes). No pass_standard was lowered and no canon predicate was removed: every widened selector or pattern names the real shipped mechanism it now accepts, labeled '(flagship dialect: ...)'. Genuine gaps remain failing by design: S2 service-worker registration, S11 Library/Q&A block absent, S12 Smart Lists operation absent. v1.2 (2026-10-22, GT-028 follow-up): S8's flagship label check learned the smart-app language law — its Today-subtitle expectation is stem-matched ('The latest real activity') instead of the fossilized 'on this page' wording the law retired; see the S8 dialect_note. No pass_standard lowered and no predicate removed in v1.2. v1.3 (2026-10-23): S1 settings-labels value 'Dark mode' renamed 'Deep black' — Shawn's standing ruling names the theme 'Deep black'; the wave-2 flagships ship that label, and the v1.2 value failed them 12/13 at the strict gate on this word alone (receipt: build_queue d34bf3a2, matched 'Public profile' + 'Notifications'). Canon follows the shipped, ruled label, as in the v1.1/v1.2 reconciliations.

evaluation.any_groups: For checks whose requirement is 'any:<group>', at least one check in that group must pass.
evaluation.feature_pass: A feature passes only when all required checks and every any-group pass.
evaluation.required: Every check whose requirement is 'required' must pass.

checks.label: At least three Settings controls
checks.selector: #settings button, #settings input, #settings select, #settings textarea, [data-feature='settings'] button, [data-feature='settings'] input

features.name: Settings
features.pass_standard: A Settings section exists, exposes at least three controls, names real preferences, and shipped script binds Settings controls to a persisted state change.
features.promise: Every app has a real Settings surface whose preference controls change state and persist it.

checks.label: Install prompt can be invoked (flagship dialect: the captured window.__osInstallPrompt is prompted from the Settings install control)

features.dialect_note: The flagship captures the install prompt in the Hub pattern (window.__osInstallPrompt, prompted from the Settings install control; appinstalled cements nayanet.installed) - judged by install-prompt-call-os. The service-worker check is NOT dialect: no serviceWorker.register ships in the flagship bytes (a manifest is linked and served, and an unregistered /sw.js is served at the origin). S2 therefore still fails until registration ships - a genuine gap, recorded by GT-028.
features.name: Install as App inside Settings
features.pass_standard: The Settings surface contains an install control, the app ships a manifest and a service worker, and script handles the install prompt or installed event.
features.promise: Install lives inside Settings, not as a pushed strip or banner.

checks.label: A message or compose control exists
checks.selector: #msgbtn, #mail button, #mail form, #mail textarea, #mail input, [data-feature='communication'] button, [data-feature='communication'] textarea, [data-feature='communication'] form, #os-msg-btn, #os-msg-body, [data-block='message'] textarea, [data-block='message'] button, [data-block='message'] form

checks.label: Message button has its own handler
Message is delivered into the Smart Mail backend tables (flagship dialect: Supabase smart_mail_threads / smart_mail_messages insert)

features.name: Working communication
features.pass_standard: A mail/message surface and a compose or message control exist, and shipped code binds that control to a mailto, message endpoint, or posting operation. A placeholder telling the user to connect mail, with no working action, fails.
features.promise: A visitor or owner can message or mail from the app and the app can deliver it to an inbox or post it to the page.

checks.label: Chosen image is read as a data URL
Script creates an image element for the new picture
Script inserts the new picture markup
Script assigns the read image to an image element

features.name: Changeable main picture
features.pass_standard: An image file input and a visible change control exist, and shipped script reads the chosen image and applies it to an image surface.
features.promise: The owner can change the cover or profile picture from the page.

checks.label: At least five main-area routes are present
Script binds the flagship rooms-plus control and opens the areas drawer (Hub twin-plus dialect)

features.dialect_note: Canon selectors name the canon-base plus (#plusbtn/#plusmenu). The flagship ships the Hub twin-plus: rooms-plus (#os-rooms-plus) opens the NayaNET areas drawer (#os-drawer, 15 Hub routes), eco-plus opens the owner menu. Same feature, Hub dialect, harvested verbatim into the flagship; both dialects are judged.
features.name: + button home
features.pass_standard: A + control and menu exist, the menu routes to at least five main areas, and script opens the menu and follows its routes.
features.promise: The + button always opens the main NayaNET areas so every app stays connected home.

features.name: About
features.pass_standard: An About section and text surface exist, edit/save controls exist, and shipped script persists the edited About text.
features.promise: Every app has an About surface the owner can edit and save.

checks.label: At least two cross-page family routes exist

Page data is read and written in shared backend tables (flagship dialect: Supabase smart_notes / smart_mail / invites tables keyed by page alias - state crosses origins through the backend, not localStorage)
A named account/page sync operation is implemented
A backend page-sync endpoint is called

features.dialect_note: The canon sync patterns name in-page channels (BroadcastChannel, postMessage). The flagship shares state through the Supabase backend keyed by page alias - cross-origin by construction - and its chrome routes to family destinations through the Hub areas drawer (#os-drawer, nayanet.live/#/hub/* routes). Both channel families are judged; a shared localStorage key alone still does not pass.
features.name: Cross-page sync
features.pass_standard: The app chrome routes to at least two family destinations and shipped code uses a real cross-page or account/backend sync channel. A shared localStorage key alone does not pass because it cannot cross app origins.
features.promise: Personal, business, and Spaces pages can reach and communicate with each other, with state carried across pages rather than trapped in one page.

checks.label: At least one Intel card is present
Script renders briefing cards into the Today list (flagship dialect: cards are rendered at runtime from live page data, so no static seed cards ship)

Briefing content is present (flagship dialect labels: the Today block names itself and carries its latest-real-activity subtitle — stem-matched, so the subtitle is verified by presence and shape; its wording follows the smart-app language law, 'in this app', formerly 'on this page')
Today is populated from the page's own backend tables (flagship dialect: loadToday merges wall posts, mail threads and invites)
A Today/Intel feed endpoint is called
Today surface names a data source

features.dialect_note: Canon labels ('Morning Briefing', 'IN A NUTSHELL') are the Hub Today room's labels, and canon cards ship as static seed markup. The flagship's Today block is the page's own pulse: labeled in its own words and rendered at runtime from live backend data. Card and label evidence is therefore grouped per dialect (any:card-evidence, any:label-dialect); the data-source requirement stands for both dialects. v1.2 (2026-10-22): the flagship subtitle's wording changed under the smart-app language law ('The latest real activity on this page' → 'The latest real activity in this app — newest first, live.'), and the strict gate honestly failed four flagship demo builds at 12/13 on the stale exact string. today-labels-os now matches the subtitle's stable stem ('The latest real activity'): the check still requires the Today block to name itself and carry its real-activity subtitle, but verifies that shape instead of fossilized wording, so lawful copy edits no longer read as a missing feature. No pass_standard lowered; the canon-dialect sibling check is unchanged.
features.name: Today's Intel
features.pass_standard: A Today's Intel section and briefing card exist, and shipped code populates the Today grid from a feed, endpoint, or owner data source. A static seeded briefing alone fails.
features.promise: The owner's own feed inputs surface as Today's Intel on the page.

checks.label: Invite email input exists
checks.selector: input[type='email'], input[name*='invite' i], input[id*='invite' i], [data-feature='smart-growth'] input

checks.label: Invite is delivered into the invites backend table (flagship dialect: hash-only recording - invitee_email_hash is stored, dry_run record-only mode, no email sent)

features.name: Smart Growth email invites
features.pass_standard: An invite surface contains an email input and an invite action, and shipped code delivers the invite through a mailto or invite endpoint.
features.promise: The owner can invite people to the page by email.

checks.label: A named report loader runs (flagship dialect: loadReports reads the page's own tables and renders the living dashboard)

features.name: Reports
features.pass_standard: An in-app Reports surface exists with report content, and shipped code loads, generates, or downloads report data. A navigation label or external route alone fails.
features.promise: Personal and business apps carry Reports with real report content or data.

checks.label: Question or owner-fill control exists
checks.selector: #library input, #library textarea, #library form, [data-feature='intelligent-library'] input, [data-feature='intelligent-library'] textarea, [data-feature='qa-library'] input, [data-feature='qa-library'] textarea

features.dialect_note: No dialect issue: the flagship body has no Library/Q&A block in any dialect (its 12 blocks are cover, wall, about, today, smart-notes, connections, lists, message, inbox, growth, reports, settings). Genuine absence - see the GT-028 assessment.
features.name: Intelligent Library / Q&A shell
features.pass_standard: An in-app Library/Q&A surface exists with a question or owner-fill control and shipped code to save, load, ask, or edit its contents. A navigation route alone fails.
features.promise: Every app ships the Intelligent Library/Q&A shell; the owner fills it in with Naya.

checks.label: Smart Lists has a list operation
Smart Mail has a working backend operation (flagship dialect: Supabase smart_mail tables)
Smart Mail has a working operation

features.dialect_note: The canon #mail selector names the Hub's Smart Mail room surface. On the flagship the Hub apps live as in-page blocks: Connections (#people, data-block='connections'), Smart Lists (#lists), Smart Mail (message + inbox blocks backed by the smart_mail tables). Predicates are scoped to those blocks. Note: the flagship's Smart Lists block ships content but no list operation in any dialect, so the lists-behavior group still fails - a genuine partial gap, recorded by GT-028.
features.name: Hub apps: Connections, Smart Lists, Smart Mail
features.pass_standard: All three surfaces exist. Connections has a bound connect action, Smart Lists has list content plus a list operation, and Smart Mail has a working message/mail operation. Any one dead surface fails the combined standard feature.
features.promise: The Hub's Connections, Smart Lists, and Smart Mail apps are present and working on the page.

checks.label: Smart Tabs unit ships in the app
Smart Tabs row is horizontally scrollable
Smart Tabs use the shared storage key
Smart Tabs emit their change event
Smart Tabs persist through local storage

features.name: Scrolling Smart Tabs
features.pass_standard: A Smart Tabs mount exists, the native unit ships, its row is horizontally scrollable (overflow-x:auto or equivalent), and tab state persists or emits its change event.
features.promise: Smart Tabs scroll horizontally across the bottom and persist from page to page.

standard_feature_contracts.status: Measurement contract using static DOM/source predicates. A PASS requires a shipped surface plus a working client-side mechanism or data operation, not a label alone. Browser-rendered geometry and authenticated back-end behaviour are stronger proofs and remain separate.
